title: Energy and Chemical Change
seo_title: Grade 11 Physical Sciences: Energy and Chemical Change Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 11 Physical Sciences: Energy and chemical change
standard_text: Energy changes in reactions related to bond energy; exothermic and endothermic reactions; heat of reaction ΔH; activation energy and the activated complex; potential energy diagrams; the effect of a catalyst. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 11, Chemistry: Energy and chemical change)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): exothermic and endothermic reactions, ΔH, activation energy, the activated complex and energy diagrams. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Exothermic: ΔH is negative. Endothermic: ΔH is positive.
key_sub: Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for a reaction.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy is absorbed to break bonds and released when new bonds form. If more energy is released than absorbed, the reaction is exothermic (ΔH is negative), such as combustion. If more is absorbed, it is endothermic (ΔH is positive), such as photosynthesis.

Activation energy is the minimum energy needed for a reaction to start. The activated complex is the unstable, high-energy arrangement of atoms at the top of the energy curve. A catalyst gives another pathway with a lower activation energy; it does not change ΔH.

Example

ΔH = −890 kJ·mol⁻¹. Exothermic or endothermic?

Sign of ΔH

Answer: exothermic

Example

Does a catalyst change ΔH?

It lowers only the hump.

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking breaking bonds releases energy.
  • Thinking a catalyst is used up.
  • Reading ΔH from the top of the curve instead of from the reactants to the products.

faq.q: Why does a match need to be struck to burn?
faq.a: Friction supplies the activation energy; after that the exothermic reaction supplies its own.
Yes; energy is released when glucose reacts with oxygen.

What is the activation energy of the forward reaction?
items.e: Ea = peak − reactants = 90 − 40 = 50 kJ.

items.q: What is the molar volume of a gas at 25 °C and 100 kPa (SLC)?
items.e: At SLC 1 mol of any gas occupies 24,8 L.

items.q: H<sub>2</sub> + F<sub>2</sub> → 2HF. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–H = 436, F–F = 158, H–F = 567. What is the energy change?
items.e: the energy change = broken − formed = 594 − 1 134 = −540 kJ.

items.q: In an energy profile diagram, what is the activation energy?
c: the energy difference between the reactants and the top of the energy barrier
the energy released by the reaction
the energy difference between reactants and products
items.e: the energy change is reactants to products; Ea is reactants to the peak.

items.q: H<sub>2</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub> → 2HBr. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–H = 436, Br–Br = 193, H–Br = 366. What is the energy change?
items.e: the energy change = broken − formed = 629 − 732 = −103 kJ.

items.q: H<sub>2</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub> → 2HCl. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–H = 436, Cl–Cl = 242, H–Cl = 431. Is the reaction exothermic or endothermic?
items.e: Broken 678 kJ − formed 862 kJ = −184 kJ.

items.q: CO<sub>2</sub> + 2H<sub>2</sub>O → CH<sub>4</sub> + 2O<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): C=O = 799, O–H = 463, C–H = 413, O=O = 498. How much energy is needed to break the bonds in the reactants?
What does the law of conservation of mass state?
c: mass always increases in a reaction
mass is not created or destroyed in a chemical reaction
products are always heavier than reactants
items.e: Atoms are rearranged, not lost.

items.q: Which energy unit is used for enthalpy changes of reactions?
c: joules per gram per kelvin only
items.e: the energy change is given per mole of reaction as written.

items.q: What is an endothermic reaction?
c: one that absorbs energy from the surroundings, so the energy change is positive
one that happens only in sunlight
one in which no bonds break
items.e: Photosynthesis and thermal decomposition are endothermic.

items.q: Which equation links amount, mass and molar mass?
items.e: Amount (mol) = mass (g) ÷ molar mass (g/mol).

items.q: 2HI → H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–I = 299, H–H = 436, I–I = 151. How much energy is released when the product bonds form?
What is the empirical formula of a compound?
c: the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms of each element
the actual number of atoms in a molecule
items.e: Glucose C₆H₁₂O₆ has the empirical formula CH₂O.

items.q: What is an exothermic reaction?
c: one that releases energy to the surroundings, so the energy change is negative
one that takes in energy, so the energy change is positive
items.e: Combustion and neutralisation are exothermic.

items.q: N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> → 2NH<sub>3</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): N≡N = 945, H–H = 436, N–H = 391. How much energy is needed to break the bonds in the reactants?
What is the specific heat capacity of water used in calorimetry?
items.e: q = m × c × ΔT.

items.q: What is the products of the complete combustion of a hydrocarbon?
items.e: Incomplete combustion can give CO and soot.

items.q: 2HI → H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub>. Bond energies (kJ/mol): H–I = 299, H–H = 436, I–I = 151. Is the reaction exothermic or endothermic?
items.e: Broken 598 kJ − formed 587 kJ = +11 kJ.

items.q: What is the mole?
c: the volume of 1 L of gas
the amount of substance containing 6,02 × 10²³ particles
items.e: This number is Avogadro's constant.

items.q: Why does raising the temperature increase the rate of reaction?
c: more particles have energy above the activation energy, and they collide more often
items.e: The effect on energy is the bigger one.

items.q: A catalyst is added to H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2HI (making hydrogen iodide) at equilibrium. What happens?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the left
the equilibrium shifts to the right
the position of equilibrium does not change; equilibrium is reached faster
items.e: A catalyst speeds up the forward and backward reactions equally.

items.q: A catalyst is added to C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (hydrating ethene) at equilibrium. What happens?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the left
the position of equilibrium does not change; equilibrium is reached faster

items.q: Which factor changes the value of K<sub>c</sub>?
items.e: K<sub>c</sub> depends only on temperature.

items.q: Why are enzymes important industrial catalysts?
c: they work at low temperatures and are very specific, saving energy
they work only at high temperature
items.e: Enzymes are used in detergents and food processing.

items.q: How does a catalyst increase the rate of reaction?
c: it gives particles more kinetic energy
it is used up in the reaction
it provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
items.e: The catalyst is unchanged at the end.

items.q: Why does the rate of reaction decrease as the reaction goes on?
c: reactants are used up, so their concentration falls
items.e: The curve levels off when a reactant runs out.

items.q: What happens to the rate of a gas reaction if the pressure is doubled?
c: it increases, because the particles are closer together
items.e: Higher pressure means higher concentration of gas.

items.q: What happens to the yield of ammonia if ammonia is removed as it forms?
c: the equilibrium shifts right, so more ammonia forms
items.e: Removing a product makes the system replace it.

items.q: Which part of the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve shows the molecules that can react?
c: the area to the left of the activation energy
the point where the curve starts
the area to the right of the activation energy
items.e: Only these molecules have enough energy.

items.q: Why are catalytic converters fitted to car exhausts?
c: they speed up the conversion of CO, NO and unburnt fuel into less harmful gases
items.e: They contain platinum, palladium and rhodium.

items.q: Iron rusts slowly and releases a little heat. What is the sign of the energy change for this change?
items.e: Energy released: the energy change < 0. Energy absorbed: the energy change > 0.

items.q: A match head flares when struck. Is this exothermic or endothermic?
items.e: Exothermic releases energy (surroundings warm up); endothermic absorbs energy.
